steps.title: Prepare BDNF master stock
steps.instruction: On ice make 0.2 % BSA by mixing 1 mL 4 % BSA with 19 mL DPBS, filter, keep 250 µL on ice; spin the 250 µg BDNF tube 1 min at max speed (18‑25 °C), resuspend in 250 µL 0.2 % BSA, aliquot two 125 µL portions into low‑protein‑binding tubes, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare BDNF working stock
steps.instruction: On ice chill 3 mL 0.2 % BSA, thaw one 125 µL BDNF master aliquot, add 2.375 mL 0.2 % BSA to a Bijoux tube, add the 125 µL BDNF master, mix gently, aliquot 80 µL per tube, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C (up to 12 mo for PeproTech, 3 mo for STEMCELL).

steps.title: Prepare NGF master stock
steps.instruction: Chill sterile‑filtered ddH₂O on ice, spin the 1 mg NGF tube at max speed, resuspend in 1 mL ddH₂O by gentle trituration, make five 200 µL aliquots in low‑protein‑binding tubes, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare NGF working stock
steps.instruction: On ice chill 2 mL 0.2 % BSA, thaw one 200 µL NGF master aliquot, add 1.8 mL 0.2 % BSA to a Bijoux tube, add the 200 µL NGF master, mix gently, aliquot 20 µL per tube, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C (up to 3 mo for Bio‑Rad or STEMCELL).

steps.title: Prepare NT‑3 master stock
steps.instruction: On ice make 0.2 % BSA (1 mL 4 % BSA + 19 mL DPBS), filter, keep 500 µL on ice; spin the 50 µg NT‑3 tube at max speed, resuspend in 50 µL chilled filtered ddH₂O, dilute with 450 µL 0.2 % BSA, make ten 50 µL aliquots in low‑protein‑binding tubes, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare NT‑3 working stock
steps.instruction: On ice chill 3 mL 0.2 % BSA, thaw one 50 µL NT‑3 master aliquot, add 4.95 mL 0.2 % BSA to a Bijoux tube, add the 50 µL NT‑3 master, mix gently, aliquot 80 µL per tube, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C (up to 3 mo for PeproTech or STEMCELL).

steps.title: Prepare Sato solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2.5 mg progesterone in 100 µL EtOH (fresh stock); dissolve 4 mg sodium selenite and 10 µL 1 N NaOH in 10 mL Neurobasal (fresh stock); dissolve 1.0 g transferrin, 160 mg putrescine and 1.0 g BSA in 100 mL Neurobasal, add 25 µL progesterone stock and 1000 µL sodium selenite stock, filter through a pre‑rinsed 0.22 µm filter, aliquot 200 µL, store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Coat BSL‑1 panning plate
steps.instruction: In a 15 cm Petri dish coat with 60 µL of 2 mg/mL BSL‑1 (diluted in 20 mL PBS), tilt and pipette up/down 2‑3 times, immediately set plate down and shake front‑back and side‑to‑side to spread evenly.

steps.title: Coat CD9 panning plate
steps.instruction: In a 15 cm Petri dish coat with 90 µL Goat‑anti‑mouse IgG+IgM (diluted in 20 mL Tris‑HCl, pH 9.5), tilt and pipette up/down 2‑3 times, set plate down and shake front‑back and side‑to‑side for even coverage.

steps.title: Incubate panning plates (first part)
steps.instruction: Place both coated plates at 4 °C for ≥16 h.

steps.title: Prepare coverslips
steps.instruction: Wash coverslips continuously in 100 % ethanol on a digital shaker at 150 rpm for 1 month (ethanol changed daily, optional to skip some changes); rinse three times with sterile water in a 15 cm dish, aspirate excess water, separate to avoid overlap, air‑dry ~10 min in a hood; add 100 µL 1× PDL‑borate drop to each, close dish lid, incubate 30 min at 18‑25 °C; remove PDL‑borate, rinse 3× with sterile water, aspirate, air‑dry; add 100 µL laminin solution (10 µL laminin in 5 mL Neurobasal) as a domed drop, close lid, incubate 37 °C for 16‑24 h without disturbance; keep coverslips in 24‑well plates for next‑day cell plating.

steps.title: Prepare DRG base media (80 mL)
steps.instruction: In a sterile 150 mL MilliporeSigma Stericup with a 0.45 µm syringe filter add: 36.76 mL DMEM, 36.76 mL Neurobasal, 800 µL insulin stock, 800 µL 100× Sodium Pyruvate, 800 µL 100× Penicillin/Streptomycin, 800 µL SATO stock, 1 600 µL NS‑21, 800 µL 100× T3 stock, 800 µL 100× L‑glutamine, 80 µL N‑acetyl‑L‑cysteine stock; vacuum‑filter, discard filter head, label bottle, screw lid, store at 4 °C up to 1 week (use 500 µL per well in a 24‑well plate).

steps.title: Prepare 0.2 % BSA solution (day‑of)
steps.instruction: Combine 1 mL 4 % BSA with 19 mL DPBS, store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare dissection plates
steps.instruction: Add 15 mL Leibovitz’s L‑15 to a 15 cm dish, 10 mL L‑15 to a 10 cm dish, and 5 mL PBS (Ca/Mg) to a 6 cm dish.

steps.title: Coat panning plates (second part)
steps.instruction: Rinse BSL‑1 plate with autoclaved PBS 3 ×, add 9 mL 0.2 % BSA; rinse CD9 plate with autoclaved PBS 3 ×, add 10 mL 0.2 % BSA plus 60 µL anti‑rat CD9 antibody, shake front‑back and side‑to‑side for even coating, incubate ≥2 h at 18‑25 °C.

steps.title: Prepare papain activation solution
steps.instruction: In a 15 mL Falcon tube combine 10 mL DPBS (no Ca/Mg) with 6 µL 1 N NaOH, place in a 37 °C water bath until warm (papain will be added later).

steps.title: Fix cultured DRG neurons (RNAscope)
steps.instruction: Prepare 4 % PFA in PBS, remove media from each well with a P1000 pipette, add 500 µL 4 % PFA per well, incubate 20 min; remove fixative, rinse 3 × with PBS, add 250 µL 50 % ethanol for 1 min, repeat with 70 % then 100 % ethanol (1 min each), replace with 1 mL fresh 100 % ethanol, store coverslips in 100 % ethanol at –20 °C (up to 6 mo).

steps.title: Perform RNAscope hybridization
steps.instruction: Follow the ACD RNAscope Multiplex Fluorescent v.2 kit (or the newer 323100 kit) per manufacturer’s instructions; after hybridization, dry cells on coverslips for 20 min at 18‑25 °C, use Protease IV (instead of Protease III) for 30 min in a humidity control tray at 18‑25 °C, then continue with the kit’s amplification and detection steps; image on a Zeiss LSM 800 confocal using Zen Blue, Tiles and Z‑stack functions.

steps.title: Set up FISHQuant analysis
steps.instruction: Install MATLAB, Fiji and Name Mangler; download the FISHQuant MATLAB code from Bitbucket; place the provided macro into Fiji.

steps.title: Split image channels with Fiji macro
steps.instruction: Create a new experiment folder with subfolders C1, C2, C3, C4; open Fiji, run the macro which prompts for the image folder and the four channel folders, selects each channel window, renames it (C1‑…, etc.), saves each as a TIFF in the corresponding folder, and closes all windows.

steps.title: Create cell outlines in FISHQuant
steps.instruction: Open MATLAB, type ‘FQ’, go to the Folders tab, select the C1 folder as ‘Folder for Images’, create an ‘Outlines’ folder, click Tools → List Directory Content, open the first image, click ‘New Cell’ and manually trace the full cell; repeat until all cells in the image are outlined, then save the outline file; repeat for every image in each channel folder (add DAPI images to the folder if using DAPI as background).

steps.title: Optimize detection settings per channel
steps.instruction: In the FISHQuant main interface click ‘Load image’, choose an image from the channel folder, click ‘Define Outlines’, draw a large outline encompassing background, click ‘Finished’, then ‘Detect’, confirm ‘allow smaller region in Z for analysis’, click ‘Perform detection’, adjust the Threshold Slider until green crosses cover all mRNA dots but no background, click ‘Apply detection’, then ‘Fit’ → ‘Apply Threshold’; save the detection settings in a uniquely named folder (e.g., ‘Detection Setting’).

steps.title: Batch‑process images with FISHQuant
steps.instruction: Click Tools → Batch Processing, load the saved detection settings, add all cell outline files, click ‘Process’, then save both the ‘Summary: Mature mRNA’ and ‘Analysis Results’ files to a new results folder.

steps.title: Rename channel files for re‑analysis
steps.instruction: Using Name Mangler (or another batch renamer) copy the C2 image filenames, replace ‘C2’ with ‘C1’, then repeat the detection‑setting load and batch‑processing steps (steps 12‑14) on the newly renamed C2 images so the same outlines can be used for the second channel.

description: The protocol below describes the steps of isolating DRG neurons from E15 rat embryos.1,2,3 The following reagents and materials need to be prepared prior to the beginning of the protocol. We suggest completing steps one day prior to the start of the procedure to ensure the success of the protocol. However, it is also feasible to do the BSL-1 or secondary antibody incubation of panning plates and laminin incubation of coverslips on the day of the immunopanning, for 2 h in a 37 °C incubator. Alternatively, the coating of panning plates with secondary antibodies can be done up to one week before the immunopanning experiment. Please refer to the key resources table for a list of reagents, and to the materials and equipment section for tables containing the recipes for preparing stock solutions for each reagent.1.Prepare BDNF master and working stock solutions (See materials and equipment setup for recipe).a.Master Stock Protocol.i.(All on ice) Make 0.2% BSA by adding 1 mL of 4% BSA to 19 mL DPBS.ii.Filter through solution and put 250 μL of 0.2% of BSA on ice.iii.Spin down the 250 μg tube of BDNF for 1 min in a tabletop centrifuge at maximum speed at 18°C–25°C then resuspend gently with 250 μL of 0.2% BSA.iv.Make two 125 μL Master Stock aliquots in Low Protein Binding Tubes.v.Flash-freeze in liquid N2 and store in −80°C.b.Working Stock Protocol.i.On ice, chill 3 mL of 0.2% BSA and thaw a 125 μL Master Stock aliquot.ii.Add 2.375 mL of 0.2% BSA into Bijoux tube.iii.Add 125 μL of BDNF Master Stock and mix gently.iv.Aliquot 80 μL of BDNF solution per tube.c.Flash-freeze in liquid N2 and store in −80°C.
